Spread re-derived independently rather than trusting the current 134-sample window's tails: docs/evidence/2026-08-04-drc-measurement-determinism.md ran two dedicated 120-sample campaigns (pinned and unpinned thread pools) specifically to characterize this KiCad-upstream artifact (issue #20048, a pointer-address-keyed std::set dedup in KiCad's own creepage DRC provider -- non-deterministic across process invocations, unreachable from any kicad-cli flag or post-processing) and found creepage's support was EXACTLY {185,186,187} in both 120-sample runs (185x27/186x58/187x35 pinned; 185x16/186x48/187x56 unpinned) -- zero samples outside a 3-value band in 240 combined draws. Every other _march-logged creepage campaign agrees on spread=2 (three consecutive integers) regardless of which 3 integers -- 199-200 (spread 1, pre-#602), 185-187, 169-171 (post-#1010), 182-184 (post-#1023, this file's current band) -- the band SHIFTS as the true violation count changes, but its WIDTH has been stable at 2 across every properly-sampled (>=40) campaign since #602. A fresh, independent 20-sample live run on the CURRENT (post-#1023) board during this fix landed entirely inside the recorded band ({183: 8, 184: 12}, n=20) before an unrelated environment reset removed the local kicad-cli install mid-campaign; see docs/evidence/2026-08-11-creepage-noise-headroom-guard-fix.md for the full accounting, including the plan to extend this run once the tool is restored. No campaign at any sample size, on any board state, in this project's history has ever observed a 4th value.

Fix chosen, and what it does NOT catch: creepage ceiling 185 -> 186 (headroom 1 -> 2, matching the measured spread exactly -- not an arbitrary buffer). The TRUE measured violation count is unchanged (182-184/134, same provenance record, no new DRC run needed for this specific correction since the board did not move) -- this is a headroom-safety-margin correction, not an admission of new violations, and is NOT 'widening a ceiling to make a gate pass': the count being gated was never wrong; only the guard's own stated safety invariant against that count was unsatisfied by an inherited arithmetic mistake. error_ceiling 1251 -> 1252 (+1, matching the single per-type creepage delta, per the sum(violations_by_type) == error_ceiling invariant this file already maintains). Stated plainly, the safety tradeoff: a real new creepage regression of 1 or 2 counts on this mains-isolation category (e.g. one additional near-zero-margin HV/SELV pad pair from a bad placement) is now indistinguishable from noise and will PASS this gate undetected -- only a regression of 3 or more counts is guaranteed to be caught. Two alternatives were considered and rejected, not merely unconsidered: (1) comparing a fresh sample against the recorded [min,max] band instead of a scalar ceiling is mathematically equivalent to zero headroom (ceiling = band max) unless the band is allowed to silently expand as new noise extremes are observed in CI -- which reintroduces the exact false-failure risk this guard exists to prevent, or, if self-expanding, becomes an unreviewed ratchet-drift that could absorb a real regression one CI run at a time with no human in the loop, worse than either alternative on a safety-relevant category. (2) taking the MINIMUM across N samples at measurement time (collapsing noise by paying CI cost instead of ceiling slack) is safety-backwards for this specific defect: KiCad's dedup artifact is understood to sometimes INCORRECTLY collapse genuinely distinct violation pairs (docs/evidence/2026-08-04-drc-measurement-determinism.md sec.2, 'Finding A'), so the minimum-of-N reading converges toward the MOST under-counted run, i.e. the LEAST complete view of the board's true violations -- the opposite of what a mains-isolation gate should optimize for, and inconsistent with this file's own established 'max + headroom' convention used for every other nondeterministic category. A maximum-of-N CI-time resample (running kicad-cli several times per invocation and taking the worst reading, still compared against a low- or zero-headroom ceiling) would be strictly safer than either the min-of-N framing or this PR's static headroom raise -- it converges toward the true undiminished count and would very likely catch even a 1-2-count regression -- but it is a larger architectural change to DrcRatchet._check_board (multi-sampling per CI run, ~7s/sample x N added wall-clock) not undertaken here; recorded as the recommended follow-up alongside the already-existing recommendation (docs/evidence/2026-08-04-drc-measurement-determinism.md sec.4, docs/evidence/2026-08-04-creepage-rust-backend-survey.md) to move creepage measurement to the deterministic temper_drc_rs backend entirely, which would eliminate this blind spot rather than bound it. Also fixed in the same commit: DrcRatchet.validate_raise_evidence's >=120-sample check was hardcoded to fire only when 'clearance' is a nondeterministic_error_types key, so a creepage-only raise (like this one) was never actually sample-count-gated by the R27 machine check despite this file's own docstring claiming otherwise -- generalized to check sample count whenever ANY category is declared nondeterministic.
